## What is an Op-Amp?
- It is a type of amplifier that
	- Comes in the form of an integrated circuit (IC)
	- Has very high open-loop voltage gain (>100,000)
	- Has very high input impedance
		- Draws very little current from the signal source
		- Very low loading effect
	- Has very low output impedance (negligible)
## Symbol, Inputs and Outputs
- Has two inputs and one output
	- $V_{in+}$ (Non inverting input)
	- $V_{in-}$ (Inverting input)
	- $V_{out}$ (Output)
## What is the open-loop and closed-loop configuration?
### Open-loop configuration
**![](data:image/png;base64,)**
- No connection between $V_{out}$ and $V_{in}$
### Close-loop configuration
**![](data:image/png;base64,)**
- A connection between $V_{out}$ and $V_{in}$, which is called a feedback loop
## Operation
- Amplifies the difference between the input signals by a factor equal to it's open loop gain ($A_{ol}$)
	- $V_{out} = A_{ol}(V_{in+} - V_{in-}$)
- When $V_{in+} > V_{in-}$, it's $V_{out}$ will be positive, and vice versa
## Highest and Lowest $V_{out}$
- Highest $V_{out}$ is approximately $V_{cc} - 1.5V$
- Lowest $V_{out}$ is approximate $V_{ee}$
## Why not open-loop?
- $A_{ol}$ is usually very high, so small differences will lead to the Op-Amp going to be stuck at the highest or lowest possible $V_{out}$, unless we want a digital signal
## Characteristics of Ideal Amplifier
- Infinite open-loop voltage gain
- Infinite input impedance
- Zero output impedance
